requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

findings.claim: The new tests never exercise ReportIfLocatedInCompilation: both inputs are valid and fully keyed, so no diagnostic reaches the wrapper. Removing its source-tree guard would leave both regression tests passing, and there is also no test proving that diagnostics for types in the current compilation are still reported.

hunches.claim: The third metadata-unsafe diagnostic site identified in the requirement remains unchanged: TypeCollector.cs:735 still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. The new reportDiagnostic wrapper cannot prevent this crash because the location argument to Diagnostic.Create is evaluated before ReportIfLocatedInCompilation is called. A metadata symbol reaching that diagnostic therefore still throws IndexOutOfRangeException, so the CS8785/AD0001 no-crash requirement is not fully addressed.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a generic value type into a metadata reference, make it trigger the type-level diagnostic whose location is obtained at TypeCollector.cs:735, and consume a closed construction of it from another compilation. Run MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on the consumer and assert that neither CS8785 nor AD0001 occurs. On this head, the empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences collection is indexed before the new diagnostic-location filter can drop the diagnostic.

hunches.claim: One of the three metadata-unsafe diagnostic paths identified in the requirement remains unchanged: TypeCollector.cs:735 still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. If that diagnostic is reached for a metadata-only symbol, the generator or analyzer can still throw IndexOutOfRangeException, so the CS8785/AD0001 failure is not comprehensively fixed.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a regression case that invokes the diagnostic path at line 735 for a type or member whose DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty (declared in a referenced assembly), run both MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, and assert that neither throws and that the app still generates GeneratedMessagePackResolver. Also verify the existing two-project closed generic struct repro.

hunches.claim: The fix leaves the third unguarded DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] access identified in the requirement. The constructor wrapper cannot prevent that crash because the index is evaluated while constructing the diagnostic, before ReportIfLocatedInCompilation is called, so a metadata symbol reaching this path can still produce CS8785/AD0001.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a metadata-reference test whose closed generic struct reaches the diagnostic at TypeCollector.cs:735, then run both the generator and analyzer and assert no IndexOutOfRangeException, CS8785, or AD0001. Running with the index replaced by FirstOrDefault() should make the test pass.

hunches.claim: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull location hardening is not covered. Every metadata-struct property in the added tests has a valid integer [Key], so the branch using GetPropertyIdentifierLocation is never entered and restoring unsafe DeclaringSyntaxReferences indexing would not fail these tests.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 remove-guard: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) -> ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive because both added metadata structs give every serialized property a non-null integer key, so this diagnostic branch is skipped

hunches.claim: The MemberNeedsKey null-location hardening is likewise untested: all properties in both metadata definitions have [Key], so the changed expression is never evaluated. A keyless public property on a metadata generic struct is the missing negative case needed to exercise this path without crashing the analyzer.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1077 remove-guard: item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() -> item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation(); expected to survive because every member in both added tests has [Key], leaving the MemberNeedsKey branch unexecuted

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Suppressing diagnostics for types and members from referenced assemblies, and documenting that their defining assemblies own those diagnostics, is deliberate behavior rather than an under-reporting defect.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed; the defining assembly owns validation and formatting, so missing diagnostics in the consuming compilation are not defects.
